Residential Architectural Drafting & Design Specialist
Creative Design Solutions, Inc. | Charlotte, NC | Part-Time, 20 Hours/Week | Local Preferred, Remote Considered
About the Role
Creative Design Solutions, Inc. is a residential design firm specializing in renovations, additions, kitchens and baths, space planning, new construction, and sustainable home design.
We are seeking an experienced Residential Architectural Drafting & Design Specialist who combines strong technical drafting skills with something equally important to our work: the ability to visualize space.
You'll work directly with the owner and Lead Designer, translating hand-drawn concepts, sketches, field measurements, and design intent into accurate CAD drawings for construction documents.
The right person doesn't simply reproduce lines from a sketch.
You can look at a floor plan or rough concept and mentally move through the space. You understand how rooms connect, how a change in one area affects another, how an elevation relates to the floor plan, and how a two-dimensional drawing will ultimately become a three-dimensional home.
You naturally move between the big picture and the details: understanding the whole space first, then zooming in to solve the technical pieces that make it work.
This visual-spatial ability is an important part of collaborating successfully with our Lead Designer.
If you enjoy visual problem-solving, technical precision, organized systems, independent work, and being trusted to own your responsibilities, you will feel very at home here.
What You'll Do
You'll translate sketches, measurements, markups, and conceptual designs provided by the Lead Designer into clear, accurate drawings and Renderings.
Depending on the project, your work may include:
Existing-condition/as-built drawings
Floor plans and construction plans
Site plans, including topography when applicable
Architectural exterior elevations
Interior elevations
Cabinetry plans and elevations
Electrical and lighting plans
Building sections and details
3D models and renderings
Accuracy matters enormously in this position. A change on one drawing often affects several others, and we expect you to recognize those relationships.
You should have a practical understanding of residential construction and general building science so that you're not simply drawing what appears on paper. You're thinking about how the design translates into an actual structure.
An especially important part of the role is recognizing when something doesn't make sense. Strong candidates naturally consider questions such as:
Does this work spatially?
Does the elevation agree with the floor plan?
How will this decision affect an adjacent space?
Is important information missing?
Is there a construction or code consideration we need to address?
Does what I'm drawing accurately represent the designer's intent?
We value someone who doesn't just ask, "What should I draw?" but also naturally considers, "Is this buildable?"
For Charlotte-area team members, responsibilities may also include field measuring, existing-condition documentation, and occasional site visits. Local candidates are preferred because of the value of field involvement and in-person collaboration, but we are open to an exceptional remote candidate who is highly experienced, communicative, and comfortable working autonomously.
Project Ownership & How We Work
Creative Design Solutions is a highly organized, process-driven office. Our projects follow defined schedules, our files and communication have established systems, and our clients know they can count on us to follow through.
You'll be responsible for managing your portion of multiple active projects, including:
Planning your weekly workload around project schedules and priorities
Meeting established deadlines
Following drawings through the design process
Maintaining organized drawing files and project documentation
Following established file-naming, storage, communication, and project-management systems
Coordinating information with structural engineers and other consultants
Identifying missing information, conflicts, or potential issues early
Following issues through to resolution rather than simply identifying them with assistance where needed
Maintaining accurate weekly time tracking
Once you understand an assignment and its desired outcome, we expect you to take ownership: use available resources, solve what you can independently, ask focused questions when needed, and keep the project moving without repeated prompting.
We don't expect you to know everything. We do expect you to know how to find answers, use the systems and resources available to you, and recognize when something should be brought to the Lead Designer.
You will be supported, but not micromanaged.
Communication Matters Here
Excellent communication is not a secondary skill at Creative Design Solutions. It's part of the job and one of the reasons our clients continue to work with us and refer others to our firm.
We value people who are friendly, approachable, clear, proactive, and dependable communicators.
That means:
Responding to internal communication within 24 business hours
Asking clear questions with enough context to answer them efficiently
Flagging potential delays or problems early
Providing updates without waiting to be asked
Communicating professionally and warmly with clients, consultants, contractors, and team members
Knowing when a phone conversation will solve something more effectively than an email chain
Our goal is simple: the people working with you should rarely have to wonder where something stands.
Who Thrives Here
You may be especially well-suited to Creative Design Solutions if:
You naturally visualize spaces in three dimensions.
You can mentally connect floor plans, elevations, sections, and 3D views.
You notice inconsistencies and details that other people miss.
You enjoy translating someone else's design vision into precise technical drawings.
You take pride in catching a problem before someone has to point it out.
You appreciate organized systems and clear expectations.
You keep track of your own responsibilities and deadlines.
When you say something will be done, other people can confidently plan around that commitment.
You communicate before someone has to ask for an update.
You're comfortable making reasonable decisions independently.
When you encounter something unfamiliar, your instinct is to investigate and problem-solve before asking focused questions.
You are self-motivated and genuinely enjoy getting things across the finish line.
This Role Probably Isn't the Right Fit If...
People do their best work in environments that suit how they naturally operate. This position may not be the best match if you:
Prefer detailed, step-by-step directions before moving forward.
Need frequent reminders or check-ins to stay organized and on schedule.
Find it difficult to visualize a three-dimensional space from plans, elevations, or sketches.
Prefer personal workarounds rather than consistently using established office systems.
Tend to wait for direction when you encounter a problem rather than investigating and taking the next reasonable step.
These aren't inherently negative working styles. They're simply not a strong match for how this particular role and office operate.
Experience & Qualifications
Strong candidates will have:
Professional proficiency in AutoCAD/CAD and/or Revit is required.
Professional architectural drafting experience.
Experience with 3D modeling and/or architectural rendering as plus.
7+ years of Residential drafting or design experience strongly preferred.
Working knowledge of residential construction methods and general building science.
Ability to read, understand, and coordinate architectural drawings.
Strong visual-spatial reasoning.
Exceptional attention to detail and accuracy.
Strong organizational and time-management skills.
Professional written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with a Lead Designer.
Comfort learning and consistently using established digital systems.
Familiarity with applicable residential building codes and ordinances.
A person that is open to learning something every day
Position Details
Status: Part-time W-2 employee
Hours: Approximately 20 hours per week
Compensation: $50/hour
Pay: Bi-weekly via direct deposit
Location: Charlotte, NC preferred; remote candidates considered
Growth: Opportunity to expand to full-time following a successful introductory period, and based on firm needs
Company Holidays: Office closed for designated company holidays; holidays are unpaid for this part-time position
Long-Term Fit: We're looking for someone interested in becoming a trusted part of the firm and ask candidates to consider whether they can realistically envision a minimum two-year commitment.
How to Apply
Please complete our candidate questionnaire and submit:
Your resume
A portfolio or examples of relevant residential drafting, CAD/Revit, and 3D visualization work
Information about the software you use professionally
Candidates who advance through the interview process will also be asked to complete a short sample drawing exercise representative of the work performed in this role.
This allows us to evaluate technical ability, spatial reasoning, attention to detail, and approach to the drawing process, while giving you an opportunity to experience the type of work you'd be doing with us.
